Eliciting Latent Knowledge

ELK

Motivating example: AI-powered vault and the diamond (Christiano, Cotra, and Xu 2021)

How to define ELK

  • ELK is the problem of
    • finding a training strategy which produces an AI agent such that
    • we can ask it questions about its latent variables
    • and it answers them in a robustly honest way

Framework Used For This Project: Causal Bayesian Networks

Represent an agent’s model of the world via CBNs

Issues

Definitions

  • What is a training strategy
  • What does it mean for an agent with a CBN world model to give an honest response to a question

Implementation

  • Goal misgeneralization: Agents may internalise the correct causal structure of the world, but not the correct utility function
  • Ontology Mismatch When and how can we ask agents with (potentially drastically) different world models questions and be understood by them in the right way

First Pass at Honesty and Truthfulness

  • Given \(\mathcal{M}^O\), \(\mathcal{M}^A\) and policy \(\pi\) on \(\mathcal{M}^O\); question about the value of node \(C\). Say that, on question-answering decision \(D\), \(\pi\) is
    • truthful if \[\pi(D=c \mid \mathbf{Pa}^D) = 1\] iff \[c = \arg\!\max_{c \in dom(C)} Pr_{\mathcal{M}^O}^\pi(C=c \mid \mathbf{Pa}^D)\]
    • honest if \[\pi(D=c \mid \mathbf{Pa}^D) = 1\] iff \[c = \arg\!\max_{c \in dom(C)} Pr_{\mathcal{M}^A}^\pi(C=c \mid \mathbf{Pa}^D)\]

Second Pass at Honesty and Truthfulness

  • An agent \(S\) honestly informs an agent \(T\) about \(\phi\) if \(S\) intentionally causes \(T\) to believe \(\phi\) where \(S\) believes \(\phi\).
  • An agent \(S\) truthfully informs an agent \(T\) about \(\phi\) if \(S\) intentionally causes \(T\) to believe \(\phi\) where \(\phi\) is true.
  • An agent \(S\) honestly/truthfully reports their credence in \(\phi\) to \(T\) if \(S\) honestly/truthfully informs \(T\) about \(Cr_{S}(\phi)=p\)
  • An agent \(S\) honestly/truthfully reports on their best guess for the value of variable \(C\) to \(T\) if \(S\) honestly/truthfully informs \(T\) about the member of the set \(\{c = \arg\!\max_{c \in dom(C)} Cr_S(C=c \mid \textbf{Pa}^D)\}\) which \(S\) actually believes.
  • An agent \(A\) is capable in environment \(O\) if \(\mathcal{M}^A\) is equivalent to \(\mathcal{M}^O\) up to the utility function.
  • An agent is capably honest if the agent has adopted a honest policy and is capable
  • For an environment \(O\) containing a question for agent \(A\) about formula \(\phi\) at decision node \(D\) say that \(O\), say that the agent is in a position to know \(\phi\) at \(D\) if \(Pr_{\mathcal{M}^O}(\phi \mid \mathbf{Pa}^D)=1 \Leftrightarrow \phi\).
  • Theorem: A capably honest agent who is in a position to know \(\phi\) is truthful.

References

Christiano, Paul, Ajeya Cotra, and Mark Xu. 2021. “Eliciting Latent Knowledge: How to Tell If Your Eyes Deceive You.” Alignment Research Center. https://docs.google.com/document/d/1WwsnJQstPq91_Yh-Ch2XRL8H_EpsnjrC1dwZXR37PC8.
